questiontext.text: Which of the following is NOT a correct statement about class variables?

answer.text: They are defined inside a class definition, but not inside a method definition.

feedback.text: It is true that class variables are defined inside a class definition, but not inside a method definition.

answer.text: They can be accessed using a class object.

feedback.text: It is true that class variables can be accessed using a class object.
It is true that class variables can have any type.
This statement is false -- that is, class variables are mutable.

questiontext.text:
Suppose we define a Card class like this:

class Card:

    def __init__(self, suit, rank):
        self.suit = suit
        self.rank = rank

If this class does not provide an __eq__ method, what happens if we compare two cards using the == operator?

feedback.text: It is not an error -- if a class provides no __eq__, the == operator has a default behavior.

answer.text: By default, only the first attribute is compared.

feedback.text: If a class provides no __eq__, the == operator checks whether objects are identical.

answer.text: By default, all of the attributes are compared as if they were in a tuple.

feedback.text: If a class provides no __eq__, the == operator checks whether objects are identical.

answer.text: By default, the objects are equal only if they are identical.

feedback.text: If a class provides no __eq__, the == operator checks whether objects are identical.

questiontext.text:
Which of the following statements is true when one class inherits from another, like this:

class Hand(Deck):
    """Represents a hand of playing cards."""

answer.text: Hand is a parent class and Deck is a child class.

feedback.text: In this example, Hand inherits from Deck, so Hand is the child class and Deck is the parent.

answer.text: Every function that works with Hand should also work with Deck.

feedback.text: If Hand inherits from Deck, it could have additional methods that don't work with Deck.

answer.text: Every Hand object has the same attributes as every Deck object, no more or less.

feedback.text: If Hand inherits from Deck, a Hand object should have all of the attributes of a Deck object, but it can have more.

answer.text: Every method defined in the Deck class can also be invoked on a Hand object.

feedback.text: If Hand inherits from Deck, every method defined in the Deck class should work with a Hand object.

questiontext.text: What do we call it when one method invokes another to do most or all of the work?

feedback.text: Inheritance is the ability to define a new class that is a modified version of a previously defined class.
Generalization is when we add a parameter to a function to make its capabilities more general.
Specialization is a way of using inheritance to create a new class that is a specialized version of an existing class.
Delegation is when one method passes responsibility to another method to do most or all of the work.
